title: The stone bridge
hookLine: Zhaozhou's bridge lets donkeys and horses cross: a teaching for everyone (Blue Cliff Record 52)

lines: ALL I SEE IS A LOG.
cards: A monk has heard for a long time about the stone bridge of Zhaozhou. So when he finally meets the teacher who shares the town's name, he can't resist a jab. I've heard so much about the stone bridge of Zhaozhou, he says.
Now that I'm here, all I see is a plain log bridge. It's a pun and a challenge: the great teacher looks ordinary up close. Zhaozhou doesn't get defensive.
He plays along. This one comes from a different collection, the Blue Cliff Record, case fifty-two.

teach.h: A SECOND COLLECTION: THE BLUE CLIFF.
teach.b: First, the collection. Until now these koan days drew on the Gateless Gate.
The Blue Cliff Record is another collection, with its own cases, verses and commentary, and Zhaozhou turns up in both; the cypress tree was his too. Second, the exchange.
In paraphrase: the monk says he sees only a log bridge.

teach.h: YOU DON'T SEE THE STONE BRIDGE.
teach.b: Zhaozhou answers, you see the log bridge, but you don't see the stone bridge. The monk takes the bait: then what is the stone bridge?
Donkeys cross, says Zhaozhou, horses cross. Third, what that opens. A bridge doesn't check who's walking on it, or ask donkeys to be horses.
It carries whatever comes. Some readers hear Zhaozhou describing his own teaching: not grand to look at, but anyone can get across.
In that reading, the plain log and the well-known stone bridge are the same thing seen two ways. Fourth, why it's gentle. The monk came to expose the teacher as ordinary.
Zhaozhou doesn't deny the log. He says the monk hasn't seen the stone bridge yet, then describes it in the plainest words he has.
A good bridge disappears under your feet; you're across before you think about it.
There's a quiet humility here, and a wide welcome: whatever traveler arrives, the bridge holds.

how: The Blue Cliff Record is studied in Rinzai Zen training alongside the Gateless Gate; its cases, with their verses and commentary, are given as koans and also taken up in teachers' talks.

o: a test a monk must pass before he may enter
Zhaozhou's plain teaching, which anyone can cross on
a well-known temple Zhaozhou built with his own hands

games.q: the stone bridge: tap the pairs.

s: Zhaozhou gets offended at the monk's jab
he plays along, and turns the plain log into the point.
Zhaozhou appears in both the Gateless Gate and the Blue Cliff Record
the cypress tree is his, and so is the stone bridge.
the bridge in his answer is only for monks
donkeys cross, horses cross: it carries whatever comes.

games.q: you're Zhaozhou. a visiting monk says your stone bridge looks like a plain log up close. how do you reply?
o: say he sees the log but not the stone bridge, and say what crosses on it.
games.why: Zhaozhou says the monk sees the log but not the stone bridge, and when asked what the stone bridge is: donkeys cross, horses cross.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you've made or know how to do, a recipe, a skill, a spare room, and someone who could use it, maybe someone you wouldn't have picked.
Picture them crossing on it and getting where they need to go, with no thanks needed. When the mind drifts, come back to the breath, carrying whatever comes.

wordCard.voice: The stone bridge. Zhaozhou's answer in case fifty-two of the Blue Cliff Record: what is the stone bridge? Donkeys cross, horses cross. A teaching anyone can walk on. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese: 'donkeys cross, horses cross', Zhaozhou's answer. Pronunciation approximates Mandarin.

carryVoice: Your line: donkeys cross. Horses cross too, and whoever comes next. A new week, begun.
